1	# Playthrough Strategy
2	
3	Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
4	its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
5	area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.
6	
7	## General Strategy
8	
9	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
10	
11	## Recruiting Units
12	
13	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
14	
15	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
16	
17	## Promoting Units
18	
19	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
20	
21	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.
22	
23	## Broad strategy notes
24	
25	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
26	
27	- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
28	- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
29	- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
30	- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
31	- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
32	- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
33	- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
34	- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
35	- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

520	**Agent notes:**
521	
522	- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
523	- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
524	- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
525	- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
526	- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
527	- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
528	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
529	- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
530	- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

541

545	
546	- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
547	- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
548	- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.
549	- Enemies seen: mage and shaman just west of the north group, brigands on the peaks between the groups, steel-lance wyverns far NE, and riders, archers and more brigands south. They reach the north group on enemy phase 1.
550	- Two ballistae sit by the south group. Wil rides one (Ride, then Attack): 14 damage. Ninian's Dance gave a second shot and killed a 24 HP archer on t1.
551	
552	s02 attempt 2 (won, turn 11):
553	
554	- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
555	- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.
556	- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
557	- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
558	- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
559	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
560	- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
561	- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
562	- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

A Bolting mage and a Purge bishop (both range 3-10) also took Eliwood to 5/21. Next time, carry both lords and hide or carry Matthew before ending t1.
584	- Recruited: Harken (Hector Talk, t19), Lv8+ Hero with Brave sword, 41 max HP, and he carried the end of the chapter. Karel never appeared. Harken walks round outside the walls and drove Merlinus off the map on t17; Merlinus left by script, unharmed as far as I saw.

Only (11,3)-style one tile touches the throne from the south.

587	- Three chests NW of the throne: Pent stood on two with a Chest key and got no Chest command. I don't know why, and I did not try the third. Pent still holds that key.
588	- Items lost: Canas's Nosferatu broke (t7), Pent's Physic broke (t30), Hawkeye's Killer axe was on its last use on t13. Healing is now only Canas's Heal (about 8 uses). Hector's Heaven Seal is greyed out at Lv18-19, so he cannot promote yet.
589	- Levels seen last: Hector 19, Pent Sage 9+, Louise Sniper 7+, Canas Druid 9, Hawkeye Berserker 9, Harken gained at least one level. Lyn stayed 13 and Eliwood 4, carried all chapter. Louise was about half HP after Kenneth's counter, then healed.

591	- Next time: 31 turns was slow but safe. The waiting at the gate for Harken (t16-19) was worth it.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

- Boss: Linus on the throne, 58 HP, Light Brand. Hawkeye got 16 hit and took heavy double hits, so do not melee him. Pent took 0 damage and did about 16 x2 at 96 hit: one counter plus one player-phase round killed him. Bait Linus with Pent.
- The final stretch was slow: the last Myrmidon and Archer sat at the shops and would not come north. Chapter ending promoted Hector to Great Lord by script. The next chapter opened straight on Preparations.
- Army at handover: Hector (full HP at last read, carrying Eliwood through the win), Hawkeye Berserker Lv17 (carrying Lyn; Silver axe nearly gone, about 4 uses, Steel axe about 20), Pent Sage about Lv19 (new Elfire about 12 uses, Bolting broken), Louise Sniper Lv10 (Silver bow about 10 uses, White gem), Vaida. Hector holds Elixir (2 left), Hammer about 11, Brave axe 4 or fewer, Heaven seal; Eliwood holds another Heaven seal, plus Rapier. No healer and no staff: buy one first. About 9,900G unspent. Save prompt: chose the highlighted Ch. 29 slot, then Save.
- My mistake on t37: blind presses hit Suspend. Resume Chapter restored the same board, so nothing was rewound. What I'd do differently: keep Canas inside the formation, and buy a spare Heal on t6.

s11 attempt 3 opening notes (written t10, 37 left, no deaths): t1 Hector rescues Eliwood, Louise rescues Lyn, Hawkeye walks west along the south bank alone. t5 Armory: sell Elysian whip (5,000G) and Door key, buy Silver bow and Silver axe. t6 Vendor next door: sell Hand axe, buy Elfire. Back with the group t9-10. Hector's Brave axe one-rounds riders, even carrying; Pent's Elfire handles sword users. Shop order is Armory left, Vendor right.

s11 picked up attempt 2 on t21 (lost, GAME OVER on t34 enemy phase: Hector died, "No! Not here! Not now..."; 21 enemies left):

- Cause: I left Hector at 28/44 in the open with archers and armor around him and used Pent to attack instead of healing. On t34 a misjudged cursor (one tile off after a kill scrolled the screen) opened the field menu and my Up then A chose End, losing Louise's turn. Heal Hector first whenever he is below about 35, and screenshot before selecting a unit.
- What worked: bait with Hawkeye on a forest and kill from 2 tiles. Pent's Elfire doubles and kills nearly everything (Hero, Knights, Generals, Warriors), Louise's Silver bow does 20+ x2, and Hector's Hammer does 28 to armor. Heal staff restores 14-31 here. Kills went 28 to 15 between t21 and t31.
- Enemy count keeps rising: 18 on t29, 21 on t30, 15 on t31, 20 on t32 (Vaida's "Here they come again" event, wyverns from the SE), 23 on t34 (archers too). Do not end up in the open around t32-34; hold a tight formation with Hector carried or on a Fort.
- Forecast targets can default to a different enemy than the one you meant; read the HP line before A. After Pent's last attack the top tome is the one he last used.
- Carrying a lord halves Spd and Skl: Hawkeye and Hector lose doubles and take doubles. Hector hit only 24 against a sword user while carrying.

s08 attempt 2, in progress (written on t10, 41 enemies left): Canas died on the t7 enemy phase beside the group. Merlinus left the map on the t9 enemy phase ("I'm leaving before all of my finest goods get stolen!") after enemies surrounded his tent, so items sent to the convoy (Elfire, Heal, Flux, Iron axe, Silver axe if sent) may be unreachable for the rest of the chapter; I have not confirmed this. Next time buy with free slots, or collect from the tent before t8. The sold Elysian whip is gone for good; no unit in the army could use it. Pent's Elfire broke on t12; Hawkeye bought a new Elfire and a Heal on t16 (4,002G left) to hand him. Vendor stock: Door key, Heal, Fire, Thunder, Elfire, Lightning, Shine, Flux. From about t15 the remaining enemies again stop advancing unless you enter their range, which gives free turns to re-arm.

s08 attempt 1 (abandoned on t22 by Suspend and Restart Chapter, after two deaths: Canas t4, Louise t21; about 30 enemies left, not a game over):

- The real constraint is weapon uses. By t21 Hawkeye's two Steel axes were 3 uses from gone (25 uses burned in about 13 turns, counters and doubles both spend them), Hand axes had broken, and Pent had used most of Elfire. Do not stand a unit where every enemy can spend its durability for free.
- Enemy count rises: 43 at the start, armor keeps coming from the NW castle until about t13, then a lull, then Vaida and about 9 wyverns from the east and NE on the t18 enemy phase. Save resources for that wave.
- Waiting pays: around t16-17 the remaining enemies stopped advancing until something entered their range.
- The gold block tiles in the north are Forts (Def +2, Avoid +20, heals): Hector on one stayed at 40-44 HP while swarmed, taking about 3-5 a hit. Enemy swords still hit him, but the Fort carried him.
- Hector's Hammer shows 29 Atk uncarried and is his best use-efficient weapon; carrying a lord drops Hit badly (Hammer 87 to 26-59 against sword users).
- Louise cannot fight (no bow anywhere, convoy has none) and died alone at 13 HP after I sent her away. Keep her behind a fighter or on a Fort. Pent then said "This is too dangerous. Let's return home," so her death appears to pull him out as well.

- Lost: Canas, on the t4 enemy phase at 18/32 HP. He was carrying Eliwood, who was dropped unhurt beside his tile. I did not see the blow; a Silver-lance Paladin (Atk 25) stood next to him afterwards. Canas held the only Heal, so there is no healer unless the staff can be recovered.
- Start: the party is on the east bank. Cavalry (Nomads, Cavaliers, a Paladin) cross the NE bridge on t2-t4 and reach anywhere, so carry the lords before ending t3 (Canas Aid covers Eliwood, Louise Aid 5 covers Lyn, Hector Aid 12). Do not leave a wounded unit on the cluster's edge.
- Pent's Elfire one-shots most of these: Myrmidons (25-26 HP), Nomads (24-25), a Javelin Cavalier (30). Hawkeye does 25-27 with Steel.
- Hector's Heaven seal is still greyed at Lv20, so level is not the blocker. Louise still has no bow and the convoy holds none.
- My blind cursor presses opened the field menu and hit Suspend on t4. Resume Chapter restored the same board, so nothing was rewound. Check the unit panel before pressing A to select.

### Chapter 30 — The Berserker

**Objectives:**

"Claim a space" (Preparations text); "Move Hector to where Kaim stands" (Status screen). Boss Kaim (Hero, Lv16, 60 HP, Atk 33, Tomahawk, range 1-2) sits at the top of the temple in the far NW. There is no Seize command: Hector chooses Wait on Kaim's tile.

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

s12 attempt 1 (WON on t14, no deaths, no restart):

- Only 3 deployment slots, and Lyn and Eliwood can be deselected. Deployed Hector, Hawkeye and Pent; it was enough. There is no shop at Preparations.
- Route: Hector went north round the cliff, Hawkeye and Pent west along the road, then all met at the temple's east stairs (t9-10), through the corridor and up the central stairs to Kaim.
- Enemies: Knights (Hector's Hammer kills in one round and they do 0 to him; some carry Axereavers), thieves (one carried a Chest key, one a Heaven seal), a Silver-axe Fighter, and mages. Elfire and poison mages poisoned Hawkeye, Pent and Hector for about 5 HP a turn, and that hurt more than any weapon. Both Elixirs went on it.
- Kaim: Hawkeye's Silver axe does 26 at about 90 hit and takes 16 back. Pent's Elfire did only 12 in total across a x2 attack, so do not rely on magic. Kaim stayed on his tile and threw his Tomahawk 2 tiles: Hector, waiting on the tile south of Hawkeye, dropped from 30 to 17.
- Chests: SW chest gave Pure water (Pent). The far NE chest was left unopened (about 5 turns' walk, Hector at 17 HP), so its contents are unknown.
- Items: Hawkeye got Kaim's Tomahawk (15 uses). A Wolf beil (30) appeared in his inventory; I did not see where it came from, and it shows greyed for him. I discarded a spare Chest key to make room; no Merlinus here, so it is gone. Heaven seals: Hector 1, and Pent had a Pure water 3 and Iron rune. A Pent-Hawkeye support level was gained on t10.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv3+ (17/49 when the map ended, Hammer about 9, Brave axe 3, Heaven seal, no Elixirs left), Hawkeye (at least 60 max HP, Silver axe 2, Steel axe 9, Tomahawk 15, Wolf beil, Chest key), Pent (Elfire 3 at t9, then at most 2 attacks' worth of uses spent, so 0-2 left and unconfirmed; no staff). Eliwood, Lyn, Louise (Silver bow 8), Nils and Vaida (Spear 3) sat out and hold what they held. About 9,900G unspent. No healer on the roster.
- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 30 slot, then Save. Narration said "Ninian is dead." Chapter 31 opens on Preparations, objective "Protect throne".
- Next time: have Hector carry or stand clear of Kaim's 2-tile range until the boss is dead, and kill poison mages first.

### Chapter 31 — Sands of Time

**Objectives:**

"Protect throne" (Preparations text); HUD counts "1/11 Turn" up to "Last Turn". The win triggers after the enemy phase of turn 11, when Ostian reinforcements arrive.

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

s13 attempt 1 (WON, survived through t11, no restart):

- Lost: Vaida, on the t9 enemy phase (death line "Oh, Prince...Zephiel..."; gone from the Unit list). Her Spear broke on counters by t4, then poison and melee wore her down.
- What won it: Hector sat on the throne (Def +2, Avoid +20) and carried Lyn from t2; Pent carried Eliwood on the west tile; Hawkeye held the south tile. Hector was never below 49. Enemies are "Morphs" with poison weapons, Flux, Luna, Nosferatu; most do little to Hector.
- Louise and Vaida start in a separate walled annex SE of the hall. I found no quick route to the throne from there and did not try one. They get swarmed from t3. Next time move weapons to them at Preparations, or bench Vaida: she had 3 Spear uses and no spare.
- Lyn was promoted with Eliwood's Heaven seal at Preparations (Trade > Use): now Blade Lord Lv1, but stats barely rose (26 HP, Str 7) and she is still fragile. Eliwood is Lv4 with 21 HP and cannot use the remaining seal below Lv10. Hector's seal has no use for him.
- Preparations Trade > List shows everyone's items and the convoy, and can take from Nils, who cannot deploy here. Hector took Nils's Elixir 3 and Hawkeye's Wolf Beil. The Wolf Beil is usable by Hector: about 23-29 damage, and it kills most Morphs in one or two hits.
- Items lost: Louise's Silver bow broke on t8, Hawkeye's Silver axe broke by t6.
- Army at handover (Pick Units list): Hector Lv6 (Wolf Beil 20, Hammer 9, Brave axe 3, Heaven seal, Elixir 3), Lyn, Eliwood, Pent, Hawkeye, Louise, Nils. Last HP read on t11, before the final enemy phase: Hawkeye 41/60 (Lv20, Steel about 6, Tomahawk about 6), Pent 33/42 (no tome or staff), Louise 28/34 (Lv12, NO BOW, holds a Swordslayer 20 she can't use, White gem). Ch. 31 Preparations list also showed Iron sword 1 (convoy), Hand axe 3, Door key and 2 Torches (owners not checked). Funds were 9,929G before the fight. No healer. BUY BOWS, TOMES AND A STAFF if any shop appears.
- Merlinus was at 6/29 on t4 and said "That does it!" on the t5 enemy phase, then left the map. I did not see what happened to him or check the convoy at 31x.
- Ending: "Accept side quest?" Yes. Save prompt: highlighted Ch. 31 slot, then Save. Start skipped the cutscene and any title card, straight to Chapter 31x Preparations, "Get supplies". Nothing pressed on the Fight option.
- Next time: stay put on the throne from t1, and read a unit's menu before pressing A for the attack.

### Chapter 31x — Battle Preparations (gaiden)

**Objectives:**

"Get supplies" (Preparations text); HUD counts "1/5 Turn". No enemies appeared. The chapter ends by itself after turn 5.

**Recruits:**

| character | starts as | recruit with / action | important condition                                                                                              |
| --------- | --------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **karla** | npc       | **bartre**            | bartre must be a **level 5+ warrior**, be deployed, talk to her, and both must survive their forced combat round |

**Agent notes:**

s14 attempt 1 (WON after t5, no deaths, no fighting). Karla not recruited: Bartre is not in the army.

- The chapter opens with funds raised by 30,000G, to 39,929G. Left over: 7,259G after a lost arena wager (last read in the arena; not re-read after yielding).
- Shops (screen tile col,row): Armories at (10,2) lances, (13,2) axes, (7,3) swords, (10,8) bows; Vendors at (1,4) tomes, (12,5) items and staves; Arena (5,7); house (13,8) only gives a hint. The house at (0,9) could not be reached from Pent's side; unvisited.
- Backing out of a shop without buying also undoes the move, so one unit can scout several shops in a turn.
- Bought: Hawkeye two Silver axes in hand, and four more 1000G axes to the convoy (Silver or Killer, a dropped press makes the split unconfirmed; check). Lyn Silver sword x2 and Killing edge, one Silver meant for Eliwood (still on Lyn). Pent Elfire x2. Louise Silver bow x2 and Killer bow. Convoy: Recover x3 (one intended, a swallowed Up doubled it twice), Restore, Elixir x2. No Mend or Physic: all healing is adjacent-only.
- Next session, at Preparations: move staves to Pent via Trade > List, a Silver sword to Eliwood, Elixirs to whoever fights away from Pent. Hawkeye's spare slots are full, with a Chest key and an old Steel axe.
- Arena: it hands out its own weapon, not your best. Pent got plain Fire, 6 damage against a Lv20 Sage hitting him for 14. Holding B yields at no HP cost, and I lost the 620G wager. Don't use it for casters.
- Levels unchanged: Hector Lv6, Hawkeye Lv20, Lyn Blade Lord low level, Eliwood Lv4 with 21 HP (too low for the seal), all at full HP as last read. Merlinus deployed, Yes, so the convoy is intact.
- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 31x slot, then Save. Chapter 32's title card did not show on any screenshot; Preparations reads "Chapter 32", objective "Seize gate".
- Next time: buy one item, screenshot, then the next. Dropped presses during "Anything else?" wasted about 4,500G.

### Chapter 32 — Victory or Death

**Objectives:**

"Seize gate" (Preparations text). The gate is the castle in the far NE with an armored boss on it; the party starts in the far SW.

**Recruits:**

| character   | starts as | recruit with / action            | important condition            |
| ----------- | --------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **renault** | ruins     | **visit the northwestern ruins** | must do so **within 11 turns** |

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 32x — The Value of Life (gaiden)

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Final Chapter — Light (two parts)

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

ACTION t24 Hawkeye: Wait on the east side of Pent. At 60/60 he is the bait, so the Morphs have to step into his axe.

content.thinking: Six Morphs are closing in with cavalry and wyverns from the south, so I'm clearing the adjacent enemies first and keeping the formation tight to protect Pent. Pent's Elfire is taking out the lance Morph north of Hector, the one touching Louise.

content.text: ACTION t25 Louise: 18 x2 at 100 hit kills the 28 HP Morph on (12,5).
ACTION t25 Hector: this Silver-lance Morph has 1 HP after last phase's counter, so 93 hit finishes it.
ACTION t25 Hawkeye: Silver axe, 26 x2 at 100 hit against 33 HP, for a clean kill on the last Morph in contact. Its return blow only lands at about 15%.

content.thinking: I'm continuing Chapter 32 from turn 26 with no deaths so far, and I'm clearing a cavalry and wyvern wave before heading for the gate. Next, I'll use Pent's Elfire on the rider and armored unit next to Louise and Hector, after checking Louise's HP.

ACTION t26 Hawkeye: Silver axe on a mounted bow Morph right below him. 32 damage against 31 HP at 80 hit, and it can't counter at melee range.
ACTION t26 Louise: Hector missed, so she finishes it. 23 x2 at 100 hit kills the 30 HP sword rider from two tiles, and that ends our turn.

content.thinking: Party is healthy on turn 27. Louise will shoot the wyvern from (12,6) since bows work well against fliers, then Hawkeye and Pent take the riders while Hector holds the group and protects the two carried lords.

ACTION t27 Hawkeye: Killer axe on the bow rider, which can't counter at melee range. 28 of its 31 HP with a 60 crit, and Pent can finish it if needed.
ACTION t27 Pent: Elfire finishes the 3 HP bow rider, removing one more attacker before the enemy phase.
ACTION t27 Hector: Attack the bow rider beside him at no risk, since it can't counter at melee range, and plug the south side of Pent.
PLAN t28: we're surrounded. Riders stand at (12,5) and (13,6), wyverns at (11,6) and (11,8). Hawkeye and Pent clear Louise's neighbors, and Louise uses whatever bow she has left.
ACTION t28 Hawkeye: Killer axe on the 4 HP sword rider touching Louise and him, at about 92% true hit.
Louise still has a fresh Silver bow and a Killer bow, which is good news.
ACTION t28 Louise: Silver bow one-shots the wyvern at (11,6), 31 against 31 HP at 100 hit, with no counter.
ACTION t28 Pent: Elfire, 32 against 30 HP at 100 hit, kills the sword rider that's on Louise.
ACTION t28 Hector: Finish the wounded wyvern, 24 against 9 HP at 89 hit, while it deals 0 back. That's the last attack of the turn.

content.thinking: It's turn 29 with no deaths so far, and I'm wrapping up this wave. Three enemies remain in contact: Hector goes after the wyvern, Hawkeye moves to (13,8) for the riders, and Pent and Louise cover from range.

content.text: ACTION t29 Hector: 25 against 8 HP at 88 hit on the wyvern, which deals 0 back, for the kill.
ACTION t29 Hawkeye: Killer axe on the bow rider, which can't counter. It's probably a hit that leaves it at 2 HP, with a 60 crit chance to end it outright.
ACTION t29 Pent: Elfire does 31 of the rider's 32 HP. It only does 2 back at a low hit rate, and Louise can finish it.
ACTION t29 Louise: Finish the 1 HP bow rider at 100 hit, which clears this wave.

content.thinking: Everyone is still alive at turn 30, so I'm clearing the incoming wave before advancing on the gate. Hector takes the western enemy, Hawkeye the southern one, and Louise and Pent cover the remaining two.

content.text: ACTION t30 Hector: Kill the 5 HP wyvern at 100 hit.
ACTION t30 Hawkeye: Killer axe on the bow rider at (13,9), with no counter at melee range.
ACTION t30 Pent: The staff menu came up because a heal is in range and nothing is left to hit from here. Top off Hawkeye on the front line.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

### Chapter 25 — Crazed Beast

**Objectives:**

**Recruits:**

**Agent notes:**

- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. # Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.

### Chapter 25 — Crazed Beast

**Objectives:**

Earn 3 points (game text). A point is scored by a unit choosing Wait on a castle gate. There are three castles: NE, N and SW.

**Recruits:**

| character  | starts as | recruit with / action | important condition             |

**Agent notes:**

- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

### Chapter 26 — Unfulfilled Heart

**Objectives:**

Survive for 11 turns (Preparations: "Survive"; HUD counts "1/11 Turn" up to "Last Turn"). The win triggers after the enemy phase of turn 11.

**Recruits:**

None.

Vaida appears here as an enemy. Do **not** kill her; she must survive this chapter to be recruitable in Chapter 29.

**Agent notes:**

- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.
- Enemies seen: mage and shaman just west of the north group, brigands on the peaks between the groups, steel-lance wyverns far NE, and riders, archers and more brigands south. They reach the north group on enemy phase 1.
- Two ballistae sit by the south group. Wil rides one (Ride, then Attack): 14 damage. Ninian's Dance gave a second shot and killed a 24 HP archer on t1.

s02 attempt 2 (won, turn 11):

- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.
- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

### Chapter 27 — Pale Flower of Darkness

**Objectives:**

**Recruits:**

| **karel**  | green npc | **hector or lyn**                                     | mutually exclusive with harken; see the note below this table |
| **harken** | enemy     | **eliwood, marcus, lowen, hector, oswin, or isadora** | mutually exclusive with karel; see the note below this table  |

Depending on various circumstances, you will only see one of the two on the map. You cannot get both.

**Agent notes:**

s03 attempt 1 (won, Hector seized on turn 31):

- Lost: Matthew, in the t1 enemy phase. I saw "Leila..." on screen, then he was off the map and off the Unit list; I did not see the blow, so the death is inferred. A Bolting mage and a Purge bishop (both range 3-10) also took Eliwood to 5/21. Next time, carry both lords and hide or carry Matthew before ending t1.
- Recruited: Harken (Hector Talk, t19), Lv8+ Hero with Brave sword, 41 max HP, and he carried the end of the chapter. Karel never appeared. Harken walks round outside the walls and drove Merlinus off the map on t17; Merlinus left by script, unharmed as far as I saw.
- Route: south gate is a Door (key needed), then the courtyard, the gap in its north wall, the long hall, west to the gap by the bishop's room, the room north of it, east through the pillar gap, the big archer court, then the gap in its north wall to the throne. Only (11,3)-style one tile touches the throne from the south.
- Long-range tomes run out. Bait them with carried lords and kill the casters over walls: Louise's silver bow reaches 2 tiles through any wall. Waves of about 10 steel-lance wyverns come down the river from t5 and die to Louise, Pent and counters.
- Three chests NW of the throne: Pent stood on two with a Chest key and got no Chest command. I don't know why, and I did not try the third. Pent still holds that key.
- Items lost: Canas's Nosferatu broke (t7), Pent's Physic broke (t30), Hawkeye's Killer axe was on its last use on t13. Healing is now only Canas's Heal (about 8 uses). Hector's Heaven Seal is greyed out at Lv18-19, so he cannot promote yet.
- Levels seen last: Hector 19, Pent Sage 9+, Louise Sniper 7+, Canas Druid 9, Hawkeye Berserker 9, Harken gained at least one level. Lyn stayed 13 and Eliwood 4, carried all chapter. Louise was about half HP after Kenneth's counter, then healed.
- Save prompt: chose the highlighted Ch. 27 slot, then Save. Deploying Merlinus was Yes; he had no effect on the fight.
- Next time: 31 turns was slow but safe. The waiting at the gate for Harken (t16-19) was worth it.

### Chapter 28 — Battle before Dawn

**Objectives:**

Guard Zephiel (Preparations text); "Protect Zephiel for 15 turns" (Status screen); HUD counts "1/15 Turn". Fog map.

**Recruits:**

| character  | starts as | recruit with / action     | important condition                                              |
| ---------- | --------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **nino**   | green npc | **hector or lyn**         | keep her alive afterward                                         |
| **jaffar** | green npc | **nino must talk to him** | both must survive ch. 28; jaffar then joins automatically in 28x |

**Agent notes:**

s04 attempt 1 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Zephiel was killed while my army was still in the north. Three enemies stood next to him at the start of t6.

- Layout: party starts in the walled north yard. East stairs lead to a corridor, whose south wall has a locked door (Door key on Canas; Hawkeye also received one at the end of t1). South of it is the north hall. From there, stairs on the east side lead round to Nino's corridor (Hector reached her tile range by t7) and the far south hall. Zephiel's room opens only on its south side, from the south hall. Walking there takes about 10 turns; enemies arrive by t5.
- Pent one-shots casters: Elfire about 26 x2 at 100%, Bolting (range 3-10) 21 x2 at 100%, even through walls. Keep Bolting and use it from the north hall on whoever reaches Zephiel. On t3 I sent Bolting to the convoy by pressing A on a full-inventory list; do not repeat.
- Louise has no bow. An enemy thief empties the chests from about t5 (Brave lance taken t5).

s04 attempt 2 (lost, GAME OVER on t5 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..." and fell): I pressed Start through the intro and skipped Preparations by accident, so no Torch and no Merlinus. Press Start once at a time and stop at the Preparations screen.

- Pent waited with Bolting on the yard's south edge (Zephiel's column, 11 rows below Hector's start), but had no target on t3 or t5: fog hides the attackers from there.
- The swordsman on the east stairs drops a Door key and a Lockpick. Harken opened the door on t3 after Hawkeye passed him a key. Bishop and Thunder mage then stand in the door on t4; Harken and Hector kill them.
- Next: Preparations first. Swap Pent forward with Formation, give him Bolting and a Torch carrier beside him, and get him into the hall by t5, near the brick strip above Zephiel's room.

s04 attempt 3 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Ursula appears in the south hall on the t6 enemy phase and hit Hector from far away, about 26 x2 with 43 max HP; he died. **Correction to my attempt 1 note above: that game over followed the same Ursula event and Hector's "No! Not here! Not now...", so it was very probably Hector's death, not Zephiel's.** Zephiel's death reads "Mother..." (attempt 2).

- This opening held Zephiel at 20/20 through t6: Preparations gave Pent Bolting and Harken the Torch and Door key; Formation put Pent on Louise's tile and Harken on the far-east blue tile (Hector cannot be moved). Harken opened the door on t2. Pent stood at the hall's south edge above Zephiel's room by t5 and shot a Swordslayer in the south hall through the walls.
- Next: have Hawkeye Rescue Hector (his menu offers it when adjacent) before ending t6, so Ursula cannot target him. Then kill her.

s07 (picked up attempt 4 on t6; lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..."):

- Carrying Hector with Hawkeye worked: Ursula never targeted him through t9. She and about 10 enemies spent t6-t9 in the south hall attacking Jaffar.
- Nino is recruitable: Hawkeye dropped Hector in her dead-end corridor on t9 and Hector talked on t10. Hector was at Lv20 on t6.
- Zephiel's killer came from fog along the west carpet and struck in one enemy phase, so a long-range shot alone cannot save him. One intruder was already 2 tiles away on t8 (Pent's Bolting killed it). Someone must be in his room by about t8, with his two open neighbour tiles (carpet side and floor side) blocked.
- Harken was not on the Unit list in attempt 4. Check that he is deployed.

s07 attempt 5 (lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; a sword enemy inside the room killed Zephiel, 20 HP, from just below his tile):

- Rush worked but was a turn or two late: Harken opened the door on t3, the hall was clear on t5, and Hawkeye and Harken reached the south hall on t8. On t9 enemies were already on Zephiel's stairs. We killed about 12 enemies with no losses. Hector and the lords in the yard were never touched.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
